title: the Sundered Sea Rising
premise: Odile Marchetti has spent his nineteen years inside the Valley of Stillness, where the guild of wardwrights keeps magic out and, they claim, the world's horrors at bay. When the border wards collapse and every star vanishes in a single night, Odile is dragged beyond the valley by a dying courier who names him heir to a binding no one else can hold. Beyond the wards he discovers the truth: the guild didn't keep magic out — it imprisoned it, and the 'king' ruling the Sundered Sea is the vessel for that escaped power, wearing its ruler like a glove. To save both worlds, Odile must unbind the king without releasing the thing beneath him, an act that will cost the valley its stillness forever and force him to choose which inheritance defines him: the guild's lies or his own name.
about_author: Edmund Kavanagh is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent a decade mapping coastlines before turning to fiction about places that refuse to stay mapped. He writes from a house on a grey northern shore, where the tide is the only clock he trusts.

chapters.title: The Night Without Stars
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. On the eve of his guild initiation, the valley's border wards shatter and every star goes dark at once. A wounded courier staggers into the Marchetti workshop, presses a cold iron sigil into Odile's hand, and dies whispering his name. Beat: terror and awe as the safe world ends.

chapters.title: What the Guild Buried
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Confronting the guildmaster, Odile learns the elders knew the wards were failing and hid it for years. The sigil is a key of inheritance — bound to his bloodline, not his training. The guild orders him to surrender it. Beat: betrayal; the first crack in everything he trusted.

chapters.title: Out of the Stillness
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Refusing to hand over the key, Odile flees through the broken border with the courier's journal. Crossing the threshold, magic floods back into him like water into lungs — painful, intoxicating, alien. Beat: disorientation and exhilaration; leaving childhood behind.

chapters.title: The Drowned Road
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Following the journal along a road half-swallowed by the rising sea, Odile meets Sera Voss, a disgraced tide-reader exiled for predicting the starless night. She confirms the sea itself is climbing toward the valley. Beat: wary alliance born of shared exile.

chapters.title: A Court of Salt and Smoke
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. In the port city of Brackhollow, Sera shows Odile how the realm lives under the king's strange peace: no storms, no tides, no change. The people are grateful and hollow-eyed. Beat: unease dressed as order; the cost of safety made visible.

chapters.title: The King Who Does Not Blink
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Summoned to court because of the sigil's resonance, Odile stands before King Aldric — and sees the wrongness: eyes that never move, a voice speaking slightly after the mouth. The thing wearing the crown knows what he carries. Beat: dread; predator and prey recognizing each other.

chapters.title: Heir to a Lie
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Imprisoned in the palace, Odile deciphers the courier's journal: his grandmother was the original binder who caged the entity beneath the wards, and the valley was her prison's anchor. His inheritance is not a gift but a debt. Beat: identity shaken; anger at being used.

chapters.title: The Tide-Reader's Bargain
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Sera trades her knowledge of hidden sea-paths to free Odile, revealing she wants access to the palace vaults where her own family's confiscated charts lie. Two inheritances, two debts. Beat: trust deepening through mutual need.

chapters.title: Beneath the Vault of Charts
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. In the vaults, Odile finds his grandmother's true grimoire and learns the unbinding rite — and its price: the binder must take the entity into themselves or destroy the anchor entirely. Beat: horror at the choice ahead; resolve hardening.

chapters.title: Hollow Bells
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. The escape triggers alarms; the city's bells ring with no sound, and the king's peace begins visibly fraying — tides lurch, fish die in fleets. Sera sees ordinary people begin to remember what feeling is. Beat: hope flickering inside catastrophe.

chapters.title: The Warden of the Wards
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Hunted to the coast, Odile is cornered by Master Corvane, his old teacher, sent to retrieve the sigil — but Corvane confesses the guild fed generations of heirs to the binding, including Odile's mother. Beat: grief weaponized; Odile spares him and gains an unwilling ally.

chapters.title: Where the Sea Remembers
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. On a drowned island shrine, Sera performs a tide-reading that shows the entity's origin: it was once the sea's own god, bound by frightened mortals. The king is not its victim but its willing host. Beat: moral complexity; the enemy is also something stolen.

chapters.title: The King's Remnant
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Through the sigil, Odile contacts the fragment of Aldric still conscious inside his own body. The king begs for death or freedom — either will do — and reveals the entity plans to use the valley's anchor to bind the whole world into stillness. Beat: urgency; the stakes become global.

chapters.title: Storm Over Brackhollow
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. The entity retaliates, drowning districts of Brackhollow to flush out the thieves. Sera leads hundreds through her secret sea-paths while the city she resented becomes the people she saves. Beat: belonging found in action, not birthright.

chapters.title: Corvane's Confession
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Corvane, dying of wounds taken in the flood, gives Odile the final component of the rite: the guild's founding seal, kept on his body for forty years. He asks forgiveness Odile cannot yet give. Beat: inherited guilt; mercy as a discipline.

chapters.title: The Long Climb
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The company crosses the mountains toward the valley, pursued by the king's still-bound soldiers. Odile trains with the grimoire, learning that the rite requires him to stand in both worlds at once — child of the valley, heir of the sea. Beat: preparation; identity integrating rather than splitting.

chapters.title: Homecoming
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile returns to the valley to find the guild in civil war between surrender and resistance. He confronts the guildmaster with the truth of his mother's death and claims leadership of the dying guild by right of blood. Beat: belonging redefined; home as something claimed, not granted.

chapters.title: The Anchor Stone
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Beneath the valley, the party reaches the anchor stone where Odile's grandmother made her binding. The entity speaks to each of them through their deepest longing, peeling away resolve. Sera nearly walks into the sea. Beat: psychological siege; the darkest hour.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. As the stars begin to return — the entity drawing power for its final act — Odile begins the rite, taking the entity into himself while freeing Aldric's remnant to die human. The valley's stillness shatters; magic floods every field and hearth. Beat: climax; sacrifice embraced without certainty of survival.

chapters.title: What Wears the Wearer
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Inside the binding, Odile faces the entity not as a monster but as a god in mourning, and offers it what the guild never did: witness instead of imprisonment. It releases him — changed, marked, alive. Beat: resolution of the internal war; compassion as victory.

chapters.title: Tides Returning
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Weeks later, real tides return to Brackhollow. Aldric is buried with honors; a regency forms. Sera is offered reinstatement and refuses it, choosing instead to chart the new, wild coasts. Beat: renewal; the world choosing motion over safety.

chapters.title: The Wardwright's New Seal
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile rebuilds the guild not as a wall but as a bridge — teaching valley folk and sea folk alike to live with magic rather than fear it. At his mother's grave, he finally forgives Corvane, the guild, and himself. Beat: quiet close; inheritance transformed into legacy.
